newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate leader aiming for April 15 budget plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate leader aiming for April 15 budget plan.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott is still aiming to have a budget blueprint crafted by the April 15 deadline, a spokeswoman said Thursday.

The spokeswoman said the Mississippi Republican told some reporters "our date was still mid-April for a budget" and that President Clinton's budget did not stand up as a "credible" proposal when analyzed by the Congressional Budget Office.
That put Republicans "in a position of providing leadership and doing what's needed, it puts them (White House) in a position of demagoguery," the spokeswoman said, relaying Lott's comments.

Lott was asked when he had proposed a panel on the consumer price index whether that was in consultation with President Clinton. "He said yes, he thought it would be received positively and would escalate to the level where a decision could be made, but that the president had not shown leadership or courage in doing that," the spokeswoman said.
On whether Senate Republicans would put together their own budget package, Lott said were were lots of options as to how they would proceed, the spokeswoman said.
House Republican leaders have said the April 15 deadline for a budget resolution would likely be missed and that it would more likely occur in May.
